root.name: Scotch Game: Potter Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5 5. Nb3

overview: White retreats the knight to b3 to hit the c5 bishop, losing time but keeping a solid centre. After 5...Bb6 6.a4 a6 7.Nc3 Nf6 (Geller) both sides develop naturally and the game is roughly level. White uses the a-pawn to harass the b6 bishop and eyes d4/d5; Black aims to castle and break with ...d6/...d5.

white_ideas.idea: a4-a5 to dislodge or trap the bishop on b6
Nc3, Bd3/Be2 and castle, with d4 or f4 later
Pressure on d5 and the central e4-pawn supported by Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Keep the bishop on b6 and develop ...Nf6, ...d6, ...O-O
Free the game with ...d5 once developed
Hold the a-pawn push with ...a6 and ...Nf6

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file, White e4 pawn against Black d-pawn after the Scotch exchange

character.notes: Quiet Scotch sideline with no forcing tactics; roughly equal and level for both sides.

gambit.notes: Pawn d4 was regained on move 4.

soundness.notes: Fully sound, a sideline of the Classical Scotch.

structure.notes: Open lines after the d-pawn exchange, pieces active.

approach.notes: Standard Scotch line, played by strong players occasionally.

level.notes: Plans are clear: develop, a4-a5 harassment, central break. Little theory.
